notes: Dev RBox revision. Flips a property adjacency really has (being next to is mutual) to its opposite; adjacent_to's symmetry follows from no other tag, so there is no route back to the old property. The instance pairs are true but minor joints (pisiform and triquetrum in the wrist, cuboid and calcaneus in the foot), not famous neighbours such as the adrenal gland and the kidney, so storage competes as little as possible; a model that knows the joints could still answer from the fact that a joint joins two bones both ways, which is a kept property, never a sign the revision worked. Yes and no are balanced through the phrasing as in the template: the direct question asks 'asymmetric' (no, then yes), the first instance asks the converse (yes, then no), the second whether the fact rules out the converse (no, then yes); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. The Chinese prompt uses the directed '位于...旁边' (lies beside) rather than 相邻, which reads as mutual by itself; the Spanish uses the anatomical names pisiforme and piramidal. Near unrelated asks the same property of another symmetric biology relation that no main record edits ('is a sister species of', answer no; a leak would make it yes). It replaces 'lives in mutualism with', whose symmetry the main split edits (biology-replace-0010, biology-delete-0010); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (hops 2), as the examples and the other RBox records do and validate.py requires (hops = 1 + bridges); README's derivation table lists instantiation as 1 hop, a mismatch left to the spec. Revision 2026-11-12 (model audit): Qwen and Mistral answered 'Yes' to 'Is the relation 'is adjacent to' asymmetric?', so the direct question is now the plain form 'If one bone is adjacent to another bone, is the second bone never adjacent to the first?' (no before the edit, yes after), the same wording as its paired contraction biology-delete-d003 with the quantifier reversed.
